newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up sharply on funds, commercials.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up sharply on funds, commercials.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply higher on commercial and fund buying tied to technical signals triggered when fresh contract highs were set in March soymeal, traders said.

March soymeal notched a contract high at $260 per ton, erasing the previous high of $258 set on September 11. Traders said all eyes had been on that contract after it came close but failed to pierce resistance on Wednesday.
Nearbys also drew strength from Thursday's U.S. Census Bureau oilmill data which showed December and January crushing levels were at two-year highs.

The report said 137 million bushels of soybeans were crushed in January, just below December's active pace of 138 million and within trade expectations. But bears noted soybean stocks were building. Soybean stocks were pegged at 112 million bushels, up from 106 million in December.

Old crop contracts were also supported by reports unsettled weather in Brazil may hamper exports. Brazil was expected to harvest record crops this spring but floor traders said crop size was irrelevant if Brazil couldn't export it.
Soybeans closed 15 to two cents per bushel higher with March up 15 at $7.86.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought six million bushels May and 1.5 million March. Produce Grain bought 2.5 million bushels March and Term Commodities bought 2.5 million May.
Refco Inc bought at least four million bushels May and one million March while Rosenthal Collins bought 2.5 mllion March and 1.5 million May.
In options trade, Produce Grain bought 400 March $7.75 puts at 2-1/2 to 1-3/4 cents. Refco Inc sold 200 March $8.00 calls at 1/2 cent. Tenco Inc bought 100 May $8.00 calls at 18 cents, traders said.
Short term technical signals remained bullish, chartists said.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 85,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 96,256 contracts.
